article.title: How Perceived Social, Emotional, and Behavioral Skills Differ Across the Life Span
article.abstract: We investigated age-related differences in perceived social, emotional, and behavioral (SEB) skills and gender variations using a large cross-sectional sample (N = 31,315, ages 10–70). Using generalized additive models (GAMs), we identified four key findings. First, modest, temporary negative age gradients emerged during early adolescence, consistent with the “disruption principle”. Second, despite this disruption, mean levels across all five domains—Self-Management, Social Engagement, Cooperation, Emotional Resilience, and Innovation—were positively associated with age, showing steep age gradients consistent with maturation during middle adolescence and early adulthood. Third, facet-level analyses uncovered significant heterogeneity in age-related patterns otherwise obscured at the domain level. Fourth, gender differences emerged: men and women varied in age-related patterns for Cooperation and Innovation, while non-binary participants—despite lower baseline levels—exhibited significantly steeper positive age gradients than male and female counterparts across several domains. Collectively, these results highlight both parallels and distinctions between SEB skill development and established personality trait principles. This comprehensive map informs future longitudinal research and the design of developmentally appropriate interventions across the lifespan.

samples.notes: Publication cohort N=31315; analytic N=30719 after excluding 596 H-prefixed IDs already represented in 0053d (590 identical 192-item profiles; six one-item differences; all ages/genders agree). Historical 0053d stays unchanged. 1475 participants retain source category Other; binary sex contrast is Male=0 Female=1 and missing for Other. Source Gender3 is retained as gender_original in individual data (1 Female; 2 Male; 3 Other). Pair N ranges 29244-30719; the current metaSEM interface uses one reference N per matrix. Age range 10-70 spans adolescence and adulthood; adult follows the agreed mixed-age convention. Use zero-order correlations; do not restrict to the GAM ethnicity-complete subset or treat age-range analyses as independent samples. No age correlations enter matrices. Recomputed BESSI facets match all released scores exactly; domains differ by at most 1.77635683940025e-15. On the original publication cohort, all ten zero-order domain correlations match Table 1 within two-decimal rounding. The available-pair matrix minimum eigenvalue is -2.9138470499438e-07; observed correlations are preserved without repair. Country is mixed based on the original reported country entries.
